To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) private sector development has become a major focus of donors' development cooperation, but (2) the concept of private sector development is highly abstract, (3) the policies that are implemented are mostly micro-level, (4) the policies implemented have been shaped by the interests of donors, (5) the policies are not coherent, (6) the policies are mostly tied aid and (7) the policies have not been evaluated.

(i) the PSD policies of the major donors have been shaped by their own private sectors and their interests; (ii) they have focused mainly on macro level conditions for private sectors in the developing countries, and on the micro level have focused mainly on the promotion of foreign investment; (iii) they have not been coherent; (iv) they have not had a significant impact on the development of private sectors in the recipient countries; (v) the PSD policies have been a major source of tied
Donor countries are using PSD as a vehicle for the promotion of their own national economic interests.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues: (1) What is the current status of the private sector in developing countries?;
the extent to which donors' policies are shaped by the interests and needs of their own economies.
the following question: What is the nature of the relationship between the state and the private sector in the process of development?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the policies are neither well conceived nor well implemented.
donors are doing a lot of PSD, but that it is not very good.
the policies and practices of PSD are a mess.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PSD policies have become a major part of donors' development assistance, but that the quality is poor, and the results disappointing.
the private sector is a key player in development, but that the private sector development policies of the donors are not.
the policies of the donors in the area of PSD are incoherent and contradictory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PSD is a complex and contested field, and that there is a need for more research and debate on the topic.
donors need to develop a more sophisticated understanding of PSD.
donors' PSD policies and practices are not well suited to the needs of developing countries.
